relevance_note: Single-patient long-term follow-up case report of GAMT deficiency with a GAMT variant: "compound heterozygosity for a GAMT frameshift variant predicted to result in a truncated protein (c.442dupC, p.Gln148ProfsX43) and a null allele".
method_note: Hand-transcribed; no script transcribed tables. Table 1 is one patient over time (rows are ages), so its cells are quoted from the age cell through the cell; Table 1 has no stacked ' / ' cells, and dose cells with two numbers (e.g. '100 150 200') were not used. Three in-scope people: the patient (single case report, rule 5 label 'patient'); her father, who was tested and carries the frameshift variant heterozygously (label 'father of patient'); and one previously published patient from Khaikin et al. [19] (label 'ref [19] patient'), included because the Discussion gives individual-level facts (symptomatic at age 1 year, treatment started at 1 year, normal development, moderate severity at baseline); no variant is printed for that person, so no variant row. The mother is mentioned only as the parent whose allele was not detected; she is not described as tested or affected, so she has no row. The three asymptomatic Stockler-Ipsiroglu et al. [12] patients and the Khaikin/Stockler-Ipsiroglu cohort counts are group-level only and get no rows. The second GAMT allele is a 'null allele' with no printed variant description, so its variant row has variant_original_string 'not reported'; its variant type is left 'not reported' (the paper calls it a null allele, not a variant class); inheritance of the null allele is 'not reported' because the mother was not tested. Seizures and 'movement disorders' are excluded from 'she had no history of movement disorders or seizures', which refers to the time of diagnosis at 15 months; the narrower checklist items dystonia, chorea and tremor were left 'not reported' rather than inferred from the broader absence. Broad-based gait and dysdiadochokinesis were recorded as stated; ataxia was not inferred. Responding to sound/turning towards noises was not taken as excluding hearing loss. Features are time-varying (developmental delay early, age-appropriate speech and cognition at 15.8 years); these are recorded as separate rows with their ages and are not treated as contradictions. Minor inconsistency: the Results say the last visit revealed 'very mild dysdiadochokinesis and axial muscular hypotonia', the Discussion says 'only mild dysdiadochokinesis'. Vital status 'alive' is taken from the report of the last visit at 15.8 years. HPO candidates are suggestions only.

functional_evidence_statement.value: RT-PCR of blood and fibroblast mRNA (with cycloheximide to block nonsense-mediated decay) detected no transcript from the maternal allele (null allele); long range PCR excluded an intragenic deletion of exons 2-6; the variant could not be detected at gDNA level and is thought to lie in regulatory regions
span: no maternal allele could be detected, indicating the presence of a null allele, which produces no RNA transcript
RT-PCR of mRNA isolated from blood and fibroblasts showed the presence of a null allele even when nonsense mediated decay was inhibited.
Long range PCR excluded an intragenic deletion in exon 2 through 6 but could not exclude a mutation/deletion in the upstream (regulatory) regions.
The variant resulting in a null allele could not be detected at the gDNA level. Most likely the causative variant is present in the transcriptional regulatory regions of GAMT.
